Draft Format

Markdown email drafts with YAML frontmatter.

Basic Format

Email drafts are plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. The frontmatter holds metadata (recipients, subject, status), and the body below the second --- is the email content written in Markdown, which gets converted to HTML when sent. 

---
to: recipient@example.com
cc: optional@example.com
bcc: hidden@example.com
subject: "Your subject line"
status: draft
from: alternate@example.com
reply_to: reply@example.com
attachments:
  - /path/to/file.pdf
---

Email body in **Markdown** format.

Frontmatter Fields

Command Description
to Recipient address(es). Required. Comma-separated for multiple.
cc Carbon copy address(es). Optional.
bcc Blind carbon copy address(es). Optional.
subject Email subject line. Required.
status Workflow state: draft, approved, or sent. Required.
from Sender address. Optional; overrides default_from from config.
reply_to Reply-to address. Optional.
attachments List of file paths to attach; a folder path attaches every file inside it. Optional.
in_reply_to Message-ID of the message this draft answers. Written by mp reply; on send, the source is marked answered.
forwarded_from Message-ID of the message this draft forwards. Written by mp forward; on send, the source is marked forwarded.
server_message_id Message-ID of the draft's copies in the server Drafts folder. Written by the daemon when it creates the draft, or at the first push of a file written by hand; leave it alone.
conflict_of Id of the draft this file is a conflict copy of. Written by the daemon; such a file is never pushed, and removing the line keeps it as a draft of its own.

Status Workflow

Drafts follow a strict workflow. Only approved emails can be sent: the send command rejects drafts that have not been approved first. These three are the whole vocabulary of status:; where a message sits (inbox, archive, sent) is a mailbox, not a status.

draft
--> mark-approved
approved
--> send
sent

After Sending

When an email is sent, the file is updated in-place. The status changes to sent, and three fields are added: sent_at (ISO 8601 timestamp), sent_via (tool version), and message_id (the RFC 822 Message-ID, used for sync deduplication). 

---
to: recipient@example.com
subject: "Project update"
status: sent
sent_at: "2026-04-22T10:30:00Z"
sent_via: "mailypoppins 0.6.0"
message_id: "<unique-id@example.com>"
---

Email body here.

A send that reached every recipient and was recorded in the outbox then moves the draft file into drafts/.retired/, where it is kept for 30 days, and removes the draft's copy from the server Drafts folder: the copy that matters lives on the server, where the outbox appends it to Sent and sync reads it back into the local store. Discarding a draft (d, mp delete) retires it the same way.

A partial send, or one the outbox store could not record, keeps the file with status: sent, because it is the only local copy left. Sending it again means editing status: back to approved by hand, because mp send refuses anything that is not approved and mp mark-approved refuses anything already sent. Trim the recipient lines first: a re-send delivers to everyone the file still lists, including the ones who already received it.

The raw RFC 822 message is also appended to the server-side Sent folder via IMAP APPEND with the \Seen flag. This is best effort: a failed APPEND is logged but does not fail the send.

Drafts on the Server

The daemon keeps a copy of every draft in the account's Drafts folder on the server, which is where Outlook, Apple Mail, the Proton app and mp on another machine see it. A save in your editor replaces that copy a couple of seconds later. The copy's server_message_id is in the draft from the moment mp creates it, so no push writes the file and an editor holding it open is not interrupted; only a file you write by hand gets the key at its first push.

The copy's body is the message as it would be sent, so a copy sent unedited from another client carries nothing more. mp keeps its own bookkeeping out of the body: the draft file rides in X-Mailypoppins-Draft-Source headers with its bcc: left out, and the Bcc travels only in the copy's own Bcc header.

Every sync, and a check once a minute between syncs, reads the server's Drafts folder back. An edit made in Outlook, Apple Mail or the Proton app is written into the draft file: the recipients, the subject and the text above the quote, converted to Markdown, while the quoted thread below <!-- mp:quote --> stays as mp wrote it. A draft edited both here and on the server keeps the server's version, and your local text is saved beside it as <name>.conflict.md to merge by hand and delete. A draft sent or deleted in another client moves to drafts/.retired/ once two syncs in a row miss its copy, and comes back if the copy does; a draft written in mp on your other machine appears here as it was written there, and a draft started in Outlook, Apple Mail or the Proton app appears as a Markdown file of its own. The server's Drafts folder is not listed as a mailbox: its drafts are the Drafts view. An approved draft that the server changed goes back to status: draft, so nothing is sent that you did not approve.

The Drafts list shows where each draft stands: synced, pending (a push is owed), conflict, or failed (the server refused the push; mp tries again fifteen minutes later, or at once after the next save). A conflict copy (conflict_of) is never pushed, and neither is a sent draft.

A draft you approve on one machine is approved on your other machine too, as long as the copy it reads is the one mp pushed, unedited and whole: an edit in Outlook, Apple Mail or the Proton app, or an attachment the copy no longer carries, brings it back as status: draft. On Proton the approval does not travel: Proton Bridge drops the headers mp's own copy carries, so the other machine sees the text and not the approval, and you approve the draft again there.

[accounts.drafts] mirror = false in config.toml keeps an account's drafts local only. Graph accounts are not mirrored yet.

Editing Drafts

A draft is edited as the file it is. The TUI suspends itself and opens the file in $EDITOR, and returns when the editor exits.

The desktop app runs a terminal editor such as Neovim inside its reader pane, with your own configuration and plugins, while the message list stays usable beside it. It picks the editor from MP_DESKTOP_EDITOR, its editor setting, $VISUAL or $EDITOR, and otherwise looks for nvim, vim and hx, also in the Homebrew directories, so a launch from the Finder finds them. Every save updates the list at once. Quitting with :wq shows the draft's preview; :q! drops only the unsaved changes and never the file, and an editor that crashes leaves the draft as last saved, with a Reopen button.

Selecting another message while the editor runs asks whether to keep editing in the background, close the editor (the draft stays), or stay. Closing the window asks whether to close the editor or stay. A GUI editor such as VS Code or Zed named in the setting opens the draft in its own window instead, and so does one in $VISUAL or $EDITOR when neither of the two names a terminal editor.

Reply Drafts

Reply drafts are created with mp reply (or r to reply, ca to reply-all, in the TUI). They record the source message in in_reply_to. The account signature (if configured) is appended to the reply area, above a <!-- mp:quote --> comment that marks the boundary with the quoted original message.

A reply goes to the message's Reply-To address, or to its sender when it has none; a reply-all also copies everyone else the message was sent to, except you. Replying to a message you sent yourself (its sender is the account's default_from) goes back to that message's recipients instead: a reply addresses its original To, and a reply-all its original To and Cc. Your own address is left out of both, unless it was the only To.

When the reply is sent, the message it answers is marked as answered, locally and on the server. The list then shows a reply arrow next to it instead of the plain read marker.

The signature is part of the draft body, so it is visible and editable before you send. The <!-- mp:quote --> marker carries no text of its own; the send path uses it to place the quoted original below your reply and strips it from every sent copy. If it is removed, the quote falls back to the end of the body. Drafts written by older versions carry {{SIGNATURE}} in the same place; it is read as the same boundary, so those drafts still send correctly. 

---
to: original-sender@example.com
subject: "Re: Original subject"
status: draft
in_reply_to: "<message-id@example.com>"
---

Your reply goes here.

-- 
Your Name

<!-- mp:quote -->

> On 2026-01-15, sender wrote:
>
> Original message text quoted here.

Forward Drafts

Forward drafts are created with mp forward (or cf in the TUI). The to: field is left empty for you to fill in. The subject gets Outlook's "FW:" prefix, unless it already starts with FW:, Fwd: or WG:, and any attachments from the original email are listed in the attachments: array with their absolute file paths. The source message is recorded in forwarded_from and is marked as forwarded once the draft goes out.

The forward is laid out as Outlook lays it out. Below your note and signature, the original's From, Sent, To, Cc and Subject stand one per line, with Cc left out when the original had none, then the original body follows. The Sent date is written as Outlook writes it, in your time zone. The sent HTML sets these labels in bold under a thin blue-grey line, as a forward written in Outlook does, whether or not the original had an HTML part. 

---
to: ""
subject: "FW: Original subject"
status: draft
forwarded_from: "<message-id@example.com>"
attachments:
  - /path/to/original-attachment.pdf
---

Your note to the recipient.

-- 
Your Name

<!-- mp:quote -->

From: Original Sender <sender@example.com>
Sent: Thursday, January 15, 2026 9:30 AM
To: you@example.com
Cc: colleague@example.com
Subject: Original subject

Original message body here.

mp forward --as-attachment (cF in the TUI and its server search, Forward as attachment in the desktop app) attaches the original as one <date>_<subject>.eml file instead of its attachments, which travel inside it with the quoted thread. As in Outlook, the body holds only your signature, with no quoted copy of the original. A server search result the local store does not hold needs no fetch first: the original is downloaded from the server for the attachment.

Signatures

A signature is one Markdown file in ~/.config/mailypoppins/signatures/, named by its file stem: work.md is the signature work. Which one an account uses by default is app state, recorded in the app's own state file at <data_dir>/state.json.

The signature is appended to the draft body when the draft is created: after the body for a new message, in the reply area above the quoted content for a reply or forward. An account with no default signature adds nothing. 

# ~/.config/mailypoppins/signatures/work.md

-- 
**Your Name**
Title | Organization
your.name@example.com

Use -s <name> to select a specific signature, or --no-signature to skip it entirely.

cs in the TUI opens the signature manager: the files with the default starred, Enter to set or clear the default, e to edit the selected one in $EDITOR, n to create, r to rename, d to delete after a confirmation. From a shell, mp signature does the same: list, show, new, edit, rename, delete and default.

In the TUI compose wizard the Signature field selects which signature the draft uses: cycle it with Up/Down (or Ctrl+n/Ctrl+p), and press e to edit the selected signature file in $EDITOR. The same field appears when you edit an existing draft's recipients (ce in Drafts): changing the selection re-splices the signature block in the draft body. The active selection is recorded in the draft's signature frontmatter field; the spliced block is wrapped in <!-- mp:sig-start --> / <!-- mp:sig-end --> comment markers, which are stripped from every sent copy and from the preview.

Attachments

A draft's attachments: field holds file paths, and any readable path works. An entry that points at a folder attaches every file directly inside it (sorted by name, subfolders and dotfiles skipped), so a batch of files can be named by one directory rather than listed one by one. Received attachments are not files: they live as blobs beside the message row in the account's store. Forwarding a message therefore materialises its attachments once, into a stable per-message directory under the account, and writes those paths into the draft, so the forward still resolves them after the original has been archived. Images the original's HTML body shows inline through a cid: reference, such as a signature's logos, are part of the body rather than attachments and are not carried; an image the body does not reference is. 

accounts/<name>/attachments/<message-id>/
  document.pdf
  image.png
---
to: recipient@example.com
subject: "FW: Document delivery"
status: draft
attachments:
  - "/home/you/.local/share/mailypoppins/accounts/work/attachments/abc@example.com/document.pdf"
  - "/home/you/Documents/cover-letter.pdf"
---

To read an attachment of a received message rather than forward it: in the TUI press to to open one in the default app (it is written to a private temp directory first) or ts to save it to a directory you choose, and from the CLI use mp save <selector> --output <dir>. To keep the whole message as a file, press te in the TUI (also on a server search result), Export .eml in the desktop app, or use mp export <selector> --output <dir>: either writes its raw RFC 822 source as <date>_<subject>.eml, which any mail client opens.
